business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Estado Español; unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state corporate registry distinction for SL vehicles)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Unitary National; statutory codification of company and AML law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Chile Advanced Framework Agreement (2023); Spain maintains an active network of 90+ BITs and 100+ DTAAs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 3, 4, 14, 25, 32-39), as amended by Ley 19/2019, de 28 de noviembre (transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843) and Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre (Crea y Crece); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de desarrollo de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 111/2021, de 23 de febrero, regulating the Registro de Titularidades Reales (arts. 3-4: UBO is any natural person with direct or indirect ownership or control exceeding 25%, or exercising control by other means); supervisory authority: SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias); SPAC listing overlay: Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión and Reglamento (UE) 2017/1129 (prospectus regime).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social (negative name clearance certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) via CIRCE portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic registry instrument for notarial use; no apostille required in Spain; apostille only if relied upon in a foreign jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each UBO, director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of country of origin (passport office, civil registry, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification of copy plus Hague Apostille; consular legalization required for issuances from non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de Antecedentes Penales (police clearance certificate) of each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministerio de Justicia (Spain) or competent judicial/police authority in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with sworn translation into Spanish by traductor jurado

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official registry extract of each corporate UBO or institutional sponsor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry (e.g., Companies House, SEC/EDGAR verification letter) or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; if issued in Spain, notarial certification of the registered extract

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Poder Notarial (Power of Attorney) granted to the incorporation agent and Spanish counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the grantor's jurisdiction or Spanish Notary if executed in Spain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization) plus sworn translation by traductor jurado

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and sworn source-of-funds statement for the SPAC escrow trust
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking bank of sponsor/subscriber (commercial or institutional)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature and bank seal; Hague Apostille if issuer is abroad; sworn translation into Spanish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Ley 10/2010 art. 14 for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates; mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Reglamento (UE) 269/2014 and all EU CFSP implementing regulations), UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the Spanish national financial intelligence list maintained by SEPBLAC and the Banco de España; OFAC SDN list is screened as prevailing international market practice and is contractually required by Spanish credit institutions holding the SPAC escrow; screening cycles must be executed at inception, at notarial signing, and within 72 hours prior to any escrow distribution; enhanced negative-media and adverse-news screening is required for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier; all results must be documented in a compliance certificate retained for the statutory 10-year period (Ley 10/2010 art. 25).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - Certification Section; online filing and status via CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) at https://www.circe.es and certificate verification at https://www.rmercantil.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be written in the Spanish Roman alphabet, preserving accents and diacritics (a-z plus ñ, ç, ü); words from non-Roman scripts must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish; names must be pronounceable in Spanish and may incorporate tokens from Romance or official EU languages; punctuation limited to ampersand, middle dot, and hyphen; numerals are permitted but must not render the name confusingly similar to a registered denomination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España or de España (requires prior authorization of the Council of Ministers)
Banco, Caja, crédito, financiero, lending (requires prior Banco de España authorization)
Seguros, reaseguros, mutualidad (requires Dirección General de Seguros prior approval)
Sociedad de inversión, fondo de pensiones, IIC (requires CNMV prior authorization)
Ministerio, Estado, Gobierno, oficial, Consejo General, Real (requires administrative license from competent ministry)
SPAC, blank-check, sociedad de adquisición, target vehicle (flagged token requiring CNMV pre-clearance under Ley 6/2023 if public-market listing is intended)
Unión Europea, UE, Naciones Unidas, ONU, España Global (institutional protection doctrines)
Identical or confusingly equivalent to any denomination existing in the RMC central index, or that misleadingly suggests a public entity, foundation, or political party
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RMC rejection, the applicant may: (i) submit up to a new alternative name within 5 business days via CIRCE; (ii) file written alegaciones with the RMC Certification Section within 15 business days of the refusal, attaching any ministerial authorization, consent letter of the conflicting holder, or trademark registration proving lawful distinctiveness; (iii) if confirmation of rejection is issued, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice within 1 month under Ley 39/2015 administrative procedure; (iv) exhaust with judicial appeal before the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Audiencia Nacional. No separate appeal fee applies, but each new name request carries the Tasa 049 statutory fee (approx. EUR 12-40).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted acceptance for a SPAC vehicle: a virtual administrative address is tolerated only where a genuine physical office in Spain exists in which management, corporate records, UBO files, and escrow documentation are available for on-site inspection; a pure virtual or registered-agent-only address fails the substance requirement of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, art. 9) and would prevent notarial constitution and CNMV/BME admission to listing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 60-70% probability within 12 months of incorporation): SEPBLAC and CNMV risk-based supervision of Medium_Risk_Enhanced blank-check vehicles, combined with Banco de España inspection of the escrow account, materially increases the probability of unannounced physical verification of the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social (name clearance certificate, Tasa 049 plus RMC fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: Tasa 049 recalibrated annually, EUR 12-35 per submitted name

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) for SL with SPAC-object clause and escrow trust provisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Notary (Colegio Notarial of the registry district)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Arancel de Notarios, Real Decreto 1426/1989, article 1 scale)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified notarial copies and notarization bundle for UBO document set
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff per folio and signature (Arancel de Notarios, article 4)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostilles (approximately 5 documents at EUR 10-25 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice - Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (apostille section)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Ministerial statutory fee per apostille (annual fee order)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation by traductor jurado of UBO, source-of-funds, and corporate registry documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traductor Jurado accredited by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional) application
Registration in the Registro de Titularidades Reales (central UBO register)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil of the province of the registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Escrow and trust account establishment with full AML KYC onboarding for SPAC gross proceeds
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish credit institution acting as escrow trustee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; comprehensive AML onboarding package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External AML/CFT risk assessment and PEP/sanctions screening (three screening cycles plus negative media report)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent AML compliance consultant qualified under Ley 10/2010

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and administrative counsel (including foreign counsel coordination and CNMV pre-clearance consultation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish law firm (member of ICAB/ICAM or applicable provincial bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed scope or hourly rate EUR 250-450)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC), especially Arts. 20-24 (notarial deed and bylaws), 58-62 (subscription and payment), 102-105 (single-member SL), 209-227 (administration and officers); Law 14/2013, of 27 September, on Support for Entrepreneurs (Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation); provincial Registro Mercantil at the registered office (deed registration); Notarial College via the Notario autorizante; CIRCE/DUE electronic incorporation window; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for tax identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificación negativa de denominación social, Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) with bylaws, registered in the Mercantile Registry, and NIF application using Modelo 036.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL requires share capital of at least EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in at incorporation and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or an in-kind valuation report before the notary. If founders elect reduced capital of EUR 1 up to EUR 3,000, the company qualifies as a Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva, with mandatory allocation of 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve until EUR 3,000 is reached. No State escrow account is required; however, a SPAC depositary or trust escrow account at an eligible Spanish or EU credit institution is commercially mandatory and is evidenced to the notary and to the CNMV.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The public deed of incorporation and its Bylaws are hereby ratified, and the subscription of the issued participations, set at a nominal value of EUR [●] each and fully paid in as shown by the deposit certificate, is approved. (2) The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS, CITY, PROVINCE], Spain, and the directors are authorized to open, maintain and operate bank, trust and escrow accounts, including the SPAC trust account. (3) [NAME] and [NAME] are appointed joint administrators of the Company with the fullest statutory powers. (4) The Chairman and the Secretary are authorized to appear before notaries, the Mercantile Registry, AEAT, CNMV and any public authority, and to remedy any formal defect required to complete formation and listing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain certification of non-conflicting corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid, via the Mercurio/CIRCE platform of the Colegio de Registradores de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit through the official name-reservation platform three to five candidate names for a Spanish SL. The Registry issues the negative name certificate, which is valid for three months. The certificate must accompany the incorporation deed and must be in the possession of the appointing notary at the time of signature.
required_dossiers: Completed name-reservation application
Identity documents (NIE or passport) of founding shareholders
List of up to five proposed SL names
Declaration of corporate purpose as SPAC/blank-check vehicle
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the request is queried due to identical or confusingly similar names, the applicant must immediately propose new candidate names; a fresh certificate is issued within one to three working days. No administrative appeal is required for this ministerial registry process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open provisional corporate bank account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish-authorised credit institution or cash desk of Banco de España; verified by the Notary Public at incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders and UBOs undergo KYC/AML onboarding; the provisional SL account is opened in the company's name and the full share capital is deposited. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit of funds dated no earlier than two months before the deed date. A SPAC should simultaneously open the regulated trust or escrow account with a depositary institution.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the negative name certificate
Draft bylaws (Estatutos)
Passport or identity document of each founder and UBO declaration per AML Law 10/2010
Capital subscription list
Proof of source of funds for the AML file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries AML/KYC documentation, complete the UBO identification file; if the account cannot be opened, deposit the funds in cash at Banco de España or rectify the ownership structure before approaching another eligible entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute public deed of incorporation and bylaws before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario autorizante in the provincial district of the registered office, in coordination with the CIRCE/DUE incorporation office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders or duly authorised agents appear before the notary and approve the Articles of Association. The notary verifies the name certificate, paid capital and legal capacity, reads the Statute, and signs the deed, releasing a first copy for registration. The application for the provisional NIF may be attached at this stage.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Bylaws in duplicate
Identity documents of all attending founders
Notarial power of attorney for corporate founders
In-kind capital valuation report, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes defects such as an expired name certificate or an unlawful clause in the bylaws, the deficient clause is corrected and the deed is re-executed before the same notary; issues concerning the Notarial College are resolved by issuing a corrected protocol deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification number from AEAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, territorial delegation or electronic office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Modelo 036 (censo de empresarios) together with the deed summary so that AEAT assigns a provisional tax identification number. The provisional NIF is required for the Mercantile Registry registration certificate and for opening operational accounts after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 tax census form
First or second copy of the public deed
DNI or NIE of the legal representative
Provisional NIF request receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT issues a requerimiento, the company must supplement the Modelo 036 declaration or execute a corrective act within ten working days; failure to respond can be cured by a new electronic submission and supporting proof of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the deed in the Mercantile Registry and obtain final NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office, coordinated with the Registro Mercantil Central databases; final NIF issuance by AEAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first copy of the deed, provisional NIF and registry tariff receipt to the provincial registry. The registrar examines the legality and formal validity of the deed and bylaws and orders the entry in the companies register. Legal personality is acquired upon registration; after inscriptions, AEAT issues the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Primera copia de la Escritura Pública de Constitución
Provisional NIF certificate
Modelo 036 with provisional NIF
Registry arancel payment receipt
Notarial verification of capital payment
Negative name certificate copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry suspends or refuses registration based on the calificación, the company may amend the bylaws, re-execute the deed before a notary, or appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month; the appeal is a full public-law remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete SPAC listing authorization and operational licensing preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores, Bolsas y Mercados Españoles, and the competent Municipal Authority for the activity licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SPAC is to be listed on BME, file the information document or prospectus with CNMV under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, obtain authorization, arrange admission to trading and appoint the depositary or escrow agent. Simultaneously apply for the municipal licence de apertura y funcionamiento for the administrative offices and register waste or emission activities in the regional environmental registry.
required_dossiers: CNMV prospectus application
Audited financial statements of the founding vehicle, if any
Bylaws and Mercantile Registry incorporation certificate
Escrow or depositary agreement for the SPAC trust account
AML compliance manual and UBO register
Municipal licence application with fire-safety project
Environmental registration declaration for the office activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CNMV issues a requerimiento of defects, remedy the prospectus within the specified supplement period; if BME rejects admission, adapt the eligibility criteria and refile; municipal licence defects are cured by technical amendments to the fire or occupancy project or through an administrative appeal against the Ayuntamiento decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industria y PYME of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Tourism for industrial aspects; Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores for SPAC public-market authorization; and the Municipal Ayuntamiento for the local activity or opening licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de admisión a negociación de valores en BME (CNMV listing authorization) and municipal 'Licencia de apertura y funcionamiento' for administrative offices.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico, Dirección General de Biodiversidad, Bosques y Desertificación, together with the regional Consejería de Medio Ambiente
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Low-impact office and financial holding activity; not listed in Annex I or Annex II of Law 21/2013 on environmental assessment. A simplified environmental inventory registration or negative environmental certificate for the office activity is sufficient; a full EIA report is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharge; sanitary wastewater must comply with the municipal sanitation ordinance; office VOC emissions from maintenance or renovation works must respect the INSST occupational exposure limits, including a time-weighted average of 0.37 ppm (0.46 mg/m3) for formaldehyde and CO2 levels below 50 ppm; e-waste, paper and hazardous office waste must be managed under Law 7/2022 on waste and Royal Decree 1055/2022 on packaging waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Attestation of fire protection compliance under Royal Decree 513/2017; low-voltage installation certificate per Royal Decree 842/2002; structural load and occupancy clearance from the municipal architect; and a workplace risk-prevention service established under Law 31/1995 with annual occupational risk evaluation and health surveillance for office personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – official portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity without permanent establishment in Spain must appoint a Spanish tax representative (art. 10 bis LGT) and apply for an NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via AEAT form 036 or 036-equivalent digital procedure, presenting the foreign corporate registration certificate, apostilled/Apostille and translated bylaws, and evidence of the constitutional act. The AEAT assigns a non-resident NIF with a 'N' prefix for entities that are not established in Spain. For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the NIF is obtained at notarial incorporation and registration with the Mercantile Registry; the provisional NIF (prefixed 'C') becomes definitive upon filing form 600/036 before the Notary, with the final NIF format consisting of a letter, eight digits, and a control character.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists. Tax classification is statutory: all Spanish-resident entities are subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at entity level. Available elections include: (i) group VIES registration and election to apply Spanish VAT Group Registration under art. 84.3 LIVA (for controlling companies with more than 50% holdings); (ii) election to file consolidated corporate tax returns under the special group regime (arts. 55-68 LIS); (iii) equity-holding entities (incl. SPACs) may elect treatment as pure holding companies, adjusting participation exemptions under the 95% dividend-and-capital-gains participation exemption (art. 21 LIS); (iv) hybrid mismatch elections under ATAD-derived rules are limited and subject to anti-deferral provisions (arts. 15bis, 23bis LGT). No discretionary pass-through election is available for an SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 – no general VAT registration threshold in Spain. Any taxable person carrying out an economic activity in Spain must register before the start of supplies, regardless of turnover. Non-established taxable persons must register via AEAT form 036/037 or the non-EU procedure, subject to an interim registration deadline. An exception applies to intra-Community distance sales from another EU member state, where the €10,000 cross-border threshold triggers the obligation to register or use the One Stop Shop (OSS).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B electronic invoicing is compulsory for all entrepreneurs and professionals under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece'), with phased implementation commencing on 1 January 2025 for all taxable persons with annual turnover over €8 million, and by 1 January 2026 for others. The system requires digital invoices in structured formats (Facturae, XML, EDIFACT) interoperable with the receiving business. Additionally, the 'Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA' (SII) is mandatory for taxpayers in the large-enterprise regime (turnover over €6 million), VAT groups, and entities in select industries: they must transmit or register transaction records (invoices issued/received, intra-Community acquisitions, importations) to AEAT via web service/API within 4 calendar days from issuance/entry (8 calendar days for the general deadline), with a consolidated pre-evaluation period of 4 calendar days. There is no digital stamping or full real-time clearance in Spain; the SII operates as near-real-time record submission without prohibition of the underlying invoice flow.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to third countries are subject to the 0% VAT rate (exempty with credit) under art. 21 LIVA, provided that the goods depart the EU customs territory and are transported by the seller or a third party on the seller's instructions. Services directly connected to export operations, international transport of goods, and ancillary services (loading, unloading, warehousing, and commissions) are eligible if evidenced. For a SPAC/blank-check entity, zero-rating typically applies only to genuine export transactions, not to financial or escrow fees; financial services are VAT-exempt without credit unless the 'international services' export condition is met. Beneficiary must be a non-EU taxable person or equivalent status, and the service must be for use outside the EU. Documentation must be retained for 4 years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration – Single Administrative Document (DUA/SAD J.3) with proof of customs admission (electronic exit summary)
Bill of Lading (origin sea), Air Waybill (air), or CMR waybill (road), showing Spain as departure and third country as destination
Proof of physical exit from EU customs territory (seal/release notification from the Spanish customs office)
Inward Remittance Certificate or evidence of payment from the non-EU buyer (when payment is received through banking rails)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Spanish Tax Agency scrutinizes export zero-ratings through cross-validation against customs exit data (SEMEGA/ESE AIS). Fraudulent or insufficient substantiation triggers: (i) immediate regularization of the undue 0% rate, converting the transaction into taxable at 21% (if domestic) or 0% with denial of the credit; (ii) late-payment interest accrual; (iii) penalty of 50% to 150% of the VAT amount evaded under arts. 191/193 LGT, increased for concealment; (iv) in criminal cases, sanction under art. 305 CP with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and six times the defrauded sum as fine; (v) retrospective clawback can extend for the 4-year statutory limitation period (art. 66 LGT), or 5 years for intra-Community transactions under special anti-fraud provisions; (vi) exclusion from CEP/VEC and the 'green channel' customs status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as monetary authority and supervisor, together with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) of the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism for foreign investment and trade statistical declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full capital and current account convertibility within the Eurozone and European Union under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. No prior exchange control authorisation is required for inward or outward payments. Profit remittances are unrestricted, subject only to tax compliance (withholding certification), AML source-of-funds verification by reporting banks, and post-transaction statistical declaration to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments (for amounts above EUR 50,000 or as required). The euro is freely convertible; non-euro transfers settle in correspondent markets without requiring Banco de España approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No legal obligation exists in Spain to surrender export proceeds or to apply a mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted freely. The sole administrative duties are the submission of the annual/quarterly commercial transaction declaration to the DGCI (for statistical balance-of-payments purposes) and the completion of the T1 customs export declaration; proceeds repatriation timelines are contractual and not regulated.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with substantive legal constraints. A non-Spanish EMI or fintech may provide payment services in Spain only under the EU passport from its home-state regulator (for EEA EMIs) or, for third-country EMIs, after authorisation or licensing by Banco de España. EMIs cannot act as full banks, cannot grant credit, and must safeguard client funds in separate accounts; they are not viable for holding SPAC trust/escrow proceeds for public-market acquisition purposes because the escrowed acquisition war chest requires a regulated credit institution with trust-grade segregation and settlement capacity. EMIs are feasible only for low-value operational payments, not for the capital escrow rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident Spanish SL used as a SPAC vehicle, a physical appearance of at least one director or senior officer is generally required during initial onboarding, or in the alternative a notarised power of attorney (public deed) granted to a local representative with powers to open the account and sign operating mandates. Remote onboarding exists for tax-resident Spanish entities with electronic ID, but cross-border SPAC structures with US- or Cayman-listed components trigger enhanced due diligence and most Tier-1 Spanish banks will require an in-person or video-identity interview, with the final decision resting on internal country-risk and business-model appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership with SPAC founders, placing agents and warrant holders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate tree for the Spanish SL and all upstream SPAC vehicles, individual beneficial ownership schedule (25%+ threshold declaration and ultimate controller), constitutional documents, share registry extract, sanctions/PEP screening report, and legal opinion on beneficial ownership under Spanish Corporate Enterprise Act and AML/KYC regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large escrow inflows from public market raising or investor subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor subscription agreements, broker/dealer placement statements, underwriting engagement letters, audited trust account statement or escrow attorney confirmation, source-of-funds breakdown, bank reference letters, and a sworn declaration of lawful origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions or counterparties (offshore financial centres, US SPAC issuers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial rationale memorandum with target acquisition pipeline, enhanced due diligence reports on counterparties, independent director resolutions approving the escrow mandate, evidence of no shell-bank relationships, and tax residence certificates to disprove tax evasion or aggressive avoidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential classification as a shell-bank or pass-through treasury entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, personnel and substance documentation, third-party service agreements (trustee, custodian, sponsor), real office or branch lease, and board minutes demonstrating operational substance and independent exercising of control.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or investor funds must be routed to a Banco de España-registered credit institution through the SWIFT network using an explicit purpose code (e.g. for subscription to SPAC equity / overseas direct investment). The Spanish bank will require the foreign investor's identity, source-of-funds documentation, the completion of the Foreign Investment Statistical Statement (or subsequent post-investment declaration to the DGCI), and compliance with EU sanctions screening. Transfers above EUR 10,000 are subject to bank-documented AML profiling; wire instructions should reference the Spanish SL, its legal entity identifier 549300ES_SL, and the specific escrow mandate, avoiding third-country shell intermediary jurisdictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and acquisition disbursements are cleared primarily by SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for payments to identified sellers/investors and by documentary or standby Letters of Credit (with UCP600 rules) for commercial transactions. For large M&A consideration payments, high-value TARGET2/EBA SEPA settlement is the intra-EU rail, while USD disbursements clear through correspondent banks in New York or via euro-dollar TARGET2. All outbound wires require the same AML/CFT evidence pack and the use of the original order institution, never a third-party paying agent, unless expressly disclosed and approved by the compliance officer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (deliverable) executed with an authorised EU bank under ISDA/EMIR-cleared master agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to the extent the counterparty is an authorised credit institution or investment firm, with no prohibited speculative netting for non-financial treasury
Cross-currency swaps for conversion of acquisition proceeds and future target cash flows, subject to EMIR margin and reporting
Foreign exchange options (OTC or exchange-traded) for hedging planned M&A settlement exposures, only on a documented treasury-risk basis

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the General Shareholders' Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of 300 to 3,000 EUR for late filing; repeated non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following approval of the annual accounts by the General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties ranging from 100 to 600 EUR per day of delay; severe cases may lead to criminal liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit if the SL exceeds two of the following: total assets exceeding EUR 2 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 4 million, or average employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation mandated; companies must update the beneficial ownership register with the Registro Mercantil upon any change in share capital, shareholders, or control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000 to 5,000 USD if audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Certain qualifying newly incorporated entities may apply a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly created entities: 15% for the first profitable period and the following period. Entities with prior-year net turnover below EUR 1 million may qualify for reduced rates under the applicable transitional regime. Tax credits may apply for qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual productions, employment, and other statutory activities. Dividends and capital gains from qualifying substantial participations may benefit from a 95% exemption, subject to participation and holding-period requirements. The participation exemption generally produces an effective 1.25% tax burden on qualifying exempt income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry; Spanish tax losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely, subject to annual utilization limits, ownership-change restrictions, anti-abuse provisions, and applicable minimum taxable-income rules. The standard annual utilization limit is generally 70% of positive taxable income, with special caps for larger taxpayers and a minimum offset amount generally available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency AEAT electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized tax representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the deadline moves to the next business day under the applicable electronic-filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal form SL, registered office, tax period dates, accounting period, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Spanish SL as the taxpayer. Report the foreign shareholder separately only where the form requires related-party, ownership, representative, or beneficial-owner information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity classification, tax regime, group membership, special regimes, newly incorporated status, and whether the entity is subject to consolidated taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned SL remains a Spanish resident corporate taxpayer if incorporated in Spain or effectively managed in Spain. Foreign ownership alone does not create a non-resident filing regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax based on statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish statutory accounts and reconcile foreign shareholder charges, acquisition costs, financing, management fees, and transaction expenses under Spanish deductibility rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary increases or decreases for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, participation exemption, interest limitation, tax credits, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply arm's-length pricing and documentation requirements to shareholder or group charges. Deductibility is not established merely because an expense is invoiced by a foreign group company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses utilized, losses generated, remaining balances, and annual utilization limitation calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of the original losses, ownership continuity, accounting records, and restrictions applicable to acquired or dormant companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, applicable statutory rate, and calculated gross corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the 25% general rate unless the entity demonstrably qualifies for a reduced or special rate. Do not apply the 15% newly created-entity rate where the entity is part of a pre-existing group or otherwise excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D, technological innovation, employment, audiovisual, foreign tax, double-taxation, and other available credits or deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes require statutory documentation and must satisfy Spanish credit limitations. Treaties do not automatically convert foreign tax into a Spanish tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments made under Modelo 202, withholding tax credits, advance payments, and other prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Spanish withholding certificates and payment references. Foreign withholding should not be entered as Spanish withholding unless a specific Spanish credit mechanism applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net liability, amount payable or refundable, direct-debit mandate, payment reference, and bank account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent may fund the payment, but the Spanish SL remains the taxpayer and must retain the payment evidence and authorization trail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions, tax group status, participation information, and other mandatory disclosures linked to the corporate return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the return with Modelo 232, transfer-pricing documentation, beneficial-owner records, and any CbCR or country-by-country notification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax due may trigger a fixed penalty generally of EUR 100, or EUR 200 where the return was required after an AEAT request, subject to statutory reductions. Late self-assessment with tax due generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay up to 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. Incorrect or incomplete returns may attract tax penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on severity, concealment, and fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payment-on-account form, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Large taxpayers and entities using the net-tax-base method follow the applicable electronic filing and payment calendar. A taxpayer with prior-period net turnover exceeding EUR 6 million is generally subject to the minimum payment-on-account rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, tax year, and filing period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF and Spanish corporate tax period, regardless of the residence of its shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax-liability method or current-period tax-base method, as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the method supported by the entity's facts, prior tax return, and statutory eligibility. Do not infer eligibility from foreign group accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant corporate tax liability or current-period tax base and statutory payment percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Spanish corporate tax amounts and adjustments. Reconcile with management accounts and the expected Modelo 200 liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, direct debit, NRC payment reference, or other authorized payment method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment is made for the Spanish SL and retain the NRC or equivalent confirmation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate statutory late-payment interest and collection surcharges. Failure to file or incorrect filing may produce fixed or percentage-based penalties depending on whether tax is due, whether AEAT has issued a prior request, and whether the conduct caused a tax shortfall.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, information return for related-party transactions and transactions with jurisdictions classified as tax havens, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the normal filing month is November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty identification, country, relationship category, transaction type, amount, and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign parent, sponsor, arranger, adviser, lender, service-provider, and group-company transactions where the statutory thresholds or categories are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate transaction amounts by category and counterparty, including specified threshold tests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consistent accounting and tax values and reconcile with the local file and general ledger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions, holdings, financing, or structures involving jurisdictions included in the applicable Spanish non-cooperative-jurisdiction framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply enhanced evidence, beneficial-ownership, substance, and business-purpose documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, incomplete filing, or inaccurate information may trigger fixed penalties under the General Tax Law and may increase audit risk, especially where the omission concerns high-value related-party transactions or non-cooperative jurisdictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 231, country-by-country report or notification, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters where the Spanish entity is the reporting entity or has a notification obligation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The country-by-country report is generally submitted within 12 months after the end of the reporting fiscal year. The notification is generally due within the statutory corporate tax return period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ultimate parent, reporting entity, multinational group, accounting period, and consolidated revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL normally files a notification rather than the report unless it is the designated reporting entity or the applicable exchange conditions are not satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, profit, taxes paid, taxes accrued, employees, tangible assets, and retained earnings by jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consolidated group data and ensure consistency with the foreign parent group's CbCR.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to provide, late provision, or materially inaccurate CbCR information may result in significant fixed and proportional penalties under Spanish tax legislation, with enhanced audit and international information-exchange consequences.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, EU directives, and tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid tax-residence certificate issued by the recipient's tax authority, confirm beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, verify limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where relevant, and retain the shareholder, holding-period, participation, and anti-abuse evidence. Apply the reduced treaty rate only where the payer can support it. If relief is unavailable at source, withhold 19% and allow the recipient to seek a refund through the applicable non-resident tax procedure. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to qualifying EU or EEA corporate parents generally holding at least 10% for the required uninterrupted one-year period, subject to anti-abuse and substance conditions. The Spanish payer must file the relevant withholding return, normally Modelo 216, and annual information return, normally Modelo 296.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish withholding rate is generally 19% for interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty rates vary by country and commonly reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15%, subject to the applicable treaty, beneficial ownership, permanent-establishment rules, and anti-abuse provisions. Qualifying interest and royalty payments to associated companies in another EU Member State may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, generally requiring qualifying corporate status, minimum 25% direct or indirect association, a minimum holding period, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse compliance. Spanish withholding reporting generally uses Modelo 216 and Modelo 296.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain does not use a single threshold for all transfer-pricing documentation. A Spanish taxpayer is generally required to maintain a local file, subject to simplified documentation and exemptions, for controlled transactions. The master-file obligation generally applies where the consolidated net turnover of the group is at least EUR 45 million. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Modelo 232 reporting thresholds also apply separately. Certain transactions with the same counterparty and category may be exempt from Modelo 232 where the statutory EUR 250,000 aggregate threshold and other conditions are satisfied; the exemption does not eliminate arm's-length or documentation obligations.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the listed methods are not reliable
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate regime identical to the UAE or Cayman Islands Economic Substance Regulations. Substance is nevertheless required under Spanish anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership principles, EU anti-tax-avoidance rules, the principal-purpose test in treaties, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, and the place-of-effective-management test. A Spanish SPAC or acquisition vehicle should maintain Spanish directors with genuine decision-making authority, appropriate personnel or outsourced functions, records, bank controls, board minutes, commercial rationale, risk assumption, and operational capacity. A registered address, nominee director, bank account, and pass-through expenses alone are inadequate substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing acquisition income, investment income, interest, fees, capital gains, or related-party benefits; fabricating expenses; maintaining parallel accounts; or intentionally understating the corporate tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties commonly range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to the tax, late-payment interest, and collection costs. Tax fraud becomes a criminal offense where the defrauded tax quota exceeds EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax period. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, subject to aggravated-offense rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto directors may incur civil and tax liability where they intentionally participate, negligently fail to prevent the infringement, or cause the company to breach its obligations. Criminal conviction may include disqualification from public office or employment. Personal imprisonment is not automatic and requires individual criminal responsibility.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming input VAT on fictitious services, circular invoices, sham advisory fees, or expenses lacking a genuine business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of improperly claimed VAT, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 100% or more depending on concealment and fraud. Serious cases may constitute criminal tax fraud where the statutory quota threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they ordered, approved, or knowingly tolerated fictitious invoicing. Criminal imprisonment, fines, and disqualification may apply to responsible individuals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length sponsor fees, acquisition fees, shareholder loans, commitment fees, management charges, interest rates, or exit allocations to shift profits out of Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, denial of deductions, withholding-tax assessments, late-payment interest, and documentation or valuation penalties may apply. Failure to maintain required documentation can trigger statutory fixed and transaction-linked penalties, with increased exposure where the adjustment causes a tax shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for a pricing adjustment but may face liability for deliberate concealment, false documentation, abusive arrangements, or failure to maintain legally required controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees to foreign recipients without withholding, without a valid residence certificate, or by applying treaty relief without beneficial-owner and anti-abuse evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, and withholding-agent penalties. Treaty relief can be denied retroactively where the recipient lacks entitlement or the arrangement is abusive.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may become jointly or subsidiarily liable where they caused the failure, acted fraudulently, or failed to remit withheld amounts. Withholding funds for personal or group use can create severe civil and criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL solely as a nominee, conduit, treaty-shopping vehicle, or pass-through entity with no genuine investment activity, governance, risk, or commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may disregard the arrangement under conflict-in-application or simulation rules, deny deductions and treaty benefits, recharacterize income, impose tax, interest, and penalties, and refer fraudulent conduct for criminal investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil, tax, insolvency, and criminal liability if they knowingly implement a sham structure. A separate Spanish economic-substance filing regime does not protect an entity lacking genuine operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, terrorist financing, and beneficial-owner concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, accepting opaque source-of-funds structures, processing unexplained escrow or SWIFT transfers, structuring transactions to avoid controls, or ignoring suspicious acquisition financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements may result in public or private reprimands, monetary penalties that can reach the higher of statutory fixed amounts, EUR 10 million, or a percentage of annual turnover where applicable, and possible authorization or management restrictions. Suspicious transactions may require reporting to SEPBLAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be sanctioned personally where they authorized, tolerated, or failed to prevent the breach. Deliberate money laundering may result in imprisonment, fines, professional disqualification, and confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Market abuse and unauthorized public offering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing SPAC securities without required prospectus or exemption, insider dealing, unlawful disclosure, market manipulation, misleading investor communications, or failure to comply with CNMV and regulated-market requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions may include substantial fines, public statements, trading or management prohibitions, and liability for investor losses. Criminal market-abuse offenses may carry imprisonment and fines where statutory elements are satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, sponsors, officers, and advisers may incur personal administrative, civil, and criminal liability for misleading disclosures, manipulation, or intentional regulatory evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing capital or dividends while insolvent, transferring assets to sponsors or related parties below market value, subordinating legitimate creditors, or incurring obligations without a credible funding plan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be rescinded, assets recovered, and directors ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit in a culpable insolvency proceeding. Civil damages, creditor claims, and criminal insolvency offenses may also arise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The insolvency court may classify the insolvency as culpable and impose disqualification from managing assets of another person, loss of rights against the insolvency estate, restitution, damages, and deficit liability. A travel ban is not an automatic tax sanction but may arise from judicial measures in exceptional insolvency or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain reliable books, failure to approve or file annual accounts, backdating board resolutions, hiding related-party transactions, or misrepresenting the availability of acquisition funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registry closure, accounting penalties, tax reassessment, shareholder or creditor claims, auditor consequences, and possible criminal liability for false accounting may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for losses caused by breach of diligence duties, may be disqualified in insolvency, and may face criminal sanctions where false accounting or document fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without distributable reserves, using capital or investor funds as dividends, making disguised distributions to sponsors, or repatriating funds before satisfying creditors and tax obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recipients may be required to repay unlawful distributions, and the company may claim damages. Tax authorities may recharacterize the payment as salary, interest, service remuneration, or a hidden distribution and assess withholding tax and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving unlawful distributions may be jointly liable with recipients for restitution and damages. Personal liability may extend to tax and insolvency liabilities where statutory conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using escrow or SWIFT transfers to conceal sanctioned counterparties, bypass bank screening, misstate payment purpose, or route acquisition funds through prohibited jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be blocked or confiscated, bank relationships terminated, and administrative or criminal sanctions imposed under applicable sanctions, AML, and payment regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and officers may face personal fines, criminal prosecution, asset confiscation, and management disqualification. Liability depends on knowledge, authorization, control, and applicable sanctions law.
